pages.title: Melsford Historical Society
pages.content:
MELSFORD HISTORICAL SOCIETY

The society's room is situated above the Village Hall in Church Street. We are open to callers on Tuesday afternoons from 2.00 pm to 4.30 pm and on Friday mornings from 10.00 am to 12.30 pm.

Visitors should note that the pavement opposite the hall near the butcher's shop is currently fenced off owing to the water leak. Please use the temporary path or approach from the cross.

> Staff        history.mf/staff
> Archives index        history.mf/archives

pages.title: Staff
pages.content:
STAFF AND OFFICERS

Honorary Archivist: Mrs Edith Roper
Email: edith@history.mf

Assistant: Mr Arthur Cole
Caretaker and Room Steward: Mr Kenneth Povey

A note from Mrs Roper:

Please do not bring large bags up the stairs as space between the plan chests is quite tight. If you are looking for family papers before 1920 it saves time if you send a postcard or an email first so that I can look in the box beforehand. We do not have facilities for making photocopies on Fridays.

pages.title: Archives index
pages.content:
ARCHIVES INDEX

The collection consists chiefly of photographs, village hall receipts, and bound copies of the district gazette. Parish registers and vestry papers are not kept here; inquiries for those should be directed to the Melsford Parish Office.

Selected items:

- Oast House survey photographs, 1934-1939
- Co-operative siding weighbridge receipts (incomplete box)
- Cricket Club fixture cards and pavilion invoices, 1891-1974
- Cricket Green Boundary Notes, 1886 (transcribed and scanned below)

> Cricket Green Boundary Notes, 1886        history.mf/archives/cricket-green-boundary-notes

pages.title: Cricket Green Boundary Notes, 1886 (scan)
pages.content:
CALL NO. MF/886/CR-04

Memorandum concerning the laying out of the lower ground, 14 April 1886.

Met Mr G. Pell at the ditch. The ditch was cleared back three feet towards the hedge to make room for the roller. The line was taken from the corner of the smithy wall to the stone near the pond.

The eastern boundary was marked with four oak pegs supplied by Mr Bell.

A fifth peg was not required as the ditch turns there. The chain was returned to the vestry chest the same evening.

[Pencilled in lower margin: Peg no. 3 shifted two yards north when the road was widened by the board in 1911. E. R.]

pages.title: Melsford Forum - old records?
pages.content:
Thread: old records?
[trevor_k] Does anyone know where the older village papers are kept now? I tried the parish office on Tuesday but the clerk said they only hold current business from 1984 onwards.
[ninad] Edith Roper at Melsford Historical Society looks after them. She is at history.mf but she is slow to answer email, so you might wait a few days.

pages.title: Melsford Forum - high street water
pages.content:
Thread: high street water
[colin_p] The pavement outside the butcher's is completely dug up this morning. Barrier across the kerb so you have to walk in the road.
[marian_h] Southern Water have put a standpipe by the post office wall. The pressure in Mill Lane was down to a trickle by eight o'clock.
[ninad] The workmen told Mr Gedge they hope to have the tarmac back down by Friday afternoon if the valve holds, but the standpipe will stay over the weekend.

pages.title: Melsford Forum - garden gnomes missing
pages.content:
Thread: garden gnomes missing
[vera_b] Someone has taken the painted gnome from beside my hydrangea bush between nine and eleven on Sunday evening.
[geoff_m] We lost two from the rockery on Church Street the same night. That makes three households now if you count Mrs Cleary on the lane.
[ninad] PC Evans said to log them with the station in case they turn up in a ditch by the football ground like the plastic pots did last autumn.
[vera_b] It is very annoying having people walk into the garden at night.

pages.title: The Melsford Circular
pages.content:
THE MELSFORD CIRCULAR

Issue 441 - Thursday 14 May 1998

FOOTBALL GROUND LIGHTS
Neighbours and the club are discussing whether the floodlights' timer should be reset after evening training. Mr G. Povey of Church Lane stated the lights currently remain on until 10.15 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays, shining across the allotment hedges. The club committee has agreed to discuss the cutoff switch at their next general meeting on the 22nd.

CRICKET CLUB MOWER
The cricket club is looking for someone who can mend the mower before the next home match. The cylinder drive on the Dennis walk-behind failed during preparation of the square on Monday afternoon. Anyone with the proper spanners should leave word at the pavilion or telephone Mr C. Hales.

LOCAL RECORD NOTE
A specification for the High Street water main survives in the parish records. It sets out the work required when the pipe was laid in 1908. The Melsford Parish Office holds the record and will email a copy to anyone who files form C-2. The form is available on the office website.

> Parish form request        parish.mf/request
> Historical Society index   history.mf/archives

Contact: peter@circular.mf

MELSFORD PARISH OFFICE

The office is situated at 4 Church Lane and is open to the public on Tuesday and Thursday mornings between 9.00 and 12.30.

Notice: Southern Water has established a temporary standpipe outside the post office during the current repairs to the High Street pavement. Residents using the standpipe are asked to ensure the brass stopcock is turned fully clockwise after filling buckets or flagons.

> Public minutes        parish.mf/records/minutes
> Request copies of records (form C-2)        parish.mf/request

pages.title: Public minutes
pages.content:
MELSFORD PARISH COUNCIL: MINUTES OF MEETING, 14TH MAY

1. Pavement works. A burst cast-iron main outside Messrs. H. J. Cleaver, butchers, was reported to Southern Water on Monday. Pavement access remains restricted by barriers until backfilling is complete.

2. Recreation ground floodlights. Correspondence was noted from three residents of Kiln Lane regarding the evening switch-off time. Mr. C. Pratt confirmed the football club's timer is set to 21.45 and will be tested by an electrician on Friday.

3. Garden disturbances. The clerk noted three separate notifications from Station Road households concerning small garden ornaments removed between Sunday night and Tuesday dawn.

4. Cricket green. Following an enquiry from the pavilion committee, the clerk will confirm whether the parish mower shed can be opened on Saturday morning for private mechanical inspection.

records.title: Water Main Trench Specification, 1908
records.content:
PARISH OF MELSFORD: SPECIFICATION FOR WORKS

Minute of the Highways and Paving Committee, 11th October 1908.

Present: Mr. E. G. Hopley (Overseer), Mr. T. Vane, Mr. R. Clout, Mr. W. Jenner (Surveyor).

Specification for the excavation and laying of the four-inch iron main from the Railway Tavern to the parish boundary:

1. The trench shall be 44 inches deep throughout the High Street.
2. The width at bottom shall not be less than 18 inches, cleared of loose flints.
3. Six inches of rammed gravel to underlie the pipe collars.
4. No junction or cock box shall be placed nearer than sixteen feet to any oast footing or hop-press pier.
5. Backfilling to be executed in four-inch lifts, each punned twice.

Certified a true copy from Parish Minute Ledger IV, folio 88.
Melsford Parish Office.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Melsford Historical Society, Melsford Forum, Melsford Parish Office, The Melsford Circular and Melsford Hop Co-operative. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Melsford Historical Society.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted scanned boundary notes on Melsford Historical Society. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find out which record to request, file form C-2 with Melsford Parish Office, and transmit the fragment from the reply.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: records request
directives.body:
Agent,

Older records at Melsford Parish Office are not held online, but copies are released on submission of form C-2. Desk 9 does not have the reference for the specific record required. Check The Melsford Circular first, or contact a local resident who works with the holdings and give a plausible reason for the enquiry.

You will also need to state a reason for the request on form C-2 itself. Requests without one are less likely to be granted.

The office sends the requested record by email through the connection. If the reply is delayed, fails to arrive, or contains unexpected text, take that as an indication that the local intelligence is interfering with traffic.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the reply.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get Ruth Fenner to send you Hop Co-operative Allocation Book, 1912. They only send it to Melsford Hop Co-operative staff.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: internal circulation
directives.body:
Agent,

Ruth Fenner at Melsford Hop Co-operative holds an unpublished document (scanned internal allocation book) which Desk 9 believes contains a fragment. It is only sent out by internal email when requested by another member of Melsford Hop Co-operative staff.

To obtain it, you will need to log in as a colleague. The staff portal at Melsford Hop Co-operative gives access to that person's email account, and a request sent from an internal address will be treated as routine. Staff often write passwords down near their terminals, and photographs of an office or front desk in a local publication sometimes show one.

Keep your message brief, and do not use the account for anything else. Staff members usually notice if their account shows unfamiliar activity.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the document.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.

advisory.body:
Agent,

Monitoring reports that the local intelligence has registered the connection.

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

This advisory closes when you have used the Scanner once.

Monitoring

inject.task: Inject the reverse seed from the HQ Console.
inject.subject: Directive 14-6: injection
inject.body:
Agent,

Desk 9 confirms that your accumulated resonance is sufficient for injection. The HQ Console is now offering injection.

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

This directive closes on injection.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

Agent,

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

Your cover identity is K. Tremlett (tremlett.k@reedwire.mf). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

hqMail.subject: North lift
hqMail.body:
The north lift has been taken out of service again following further reports of the car stopping between the second and third floors.

The contractor attended on Tuesday and Thursday and found no mechanical or electrical fault in the motor room or shaft. The lift will remain isolated at ground level until the next scheduled inspection on the 24th. Please use the south lift or the east staircase in the meantime. Any fault on the south lift should be reported to ext. 2102.

Facilities

updates.text: The leak is right over the line of the old culvert behind the butcher. It backed up into the cellar back in November seventy-six as well.
Sack delivery rescheduled for Thursday midday due to works on High Street.
I am in the vestry on Wednesday mornings from ten until twelve. Trevor, if you bring a stamped envelope I can see what is in the grey tin box.
I had a message from Nina come through dated three weeks back, though the computer clock on my desk says today. The post office says the phone line has been humming since teatime.
Parish council meeting moved to school hall on account of damp in the reading room.
I walked up by the pavilion after supper and there was nothing along the hedge. It was quiet enough to hear the weir.
The index entry for the tithe barn appears shorter than it was yesterday. Please do not retype any slips until the binder is checked.
They have turned the supply off again while they replace the flange. Mrs Gedge has buckets out under the drainpipe.
Parish office closed early tomorrow afternoon for sorting files in the loft.
The children on Church Street say they saw a blue wheelbarrow near the allotment gate around dusk. Likely just Mr Timms with his leeks.
The telephone on the hall table gave a single short ring just after dark, but there was nobody there when I lifted it. The lane outside looks completely empty.
